answer: Pseudonym parties: credentials renew only at in-person events held worldwide in the same hour, say in a park grove or a hall. Organizers check that each attendee stays in the room until the hour ends, then sign one fresh token per person present. Since all events overlap, a person can attend only one, so each extra identity needs another real human in a room; splitting accounts cannot beat the clock. Limitation: colluding organizers can inflate counts, so random outside observers must audit, and a gale or travel cost can shut out honest people; it is a policy, not a sonnet.
